name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Two fixes for the most common playback complaints: streaming that glitches/stutters once it starts, and movies that take a long time to start playing. Proxy-mode relaying (Services/FederationStreamHandler) no longer forces a flush after every ~80KB chunk it relays (unnecessary per-chunk overhead that showed up as jitter), gained a 20s idle-read timeout so a stalled remote read fails fast instead of hanging for up to the shared 3-hour HttpClient timeout, and now resumes with a Range request from the last byte actually delivered (up to 2 retries) instead of killing the whole stream on a stall or dropped connection. Separately, FederationMediaSourceProvider was making a live, synchronous, unparallelized remote PlaybackInfo call per federated source on every single play - not just the first - and would re-resolve a fallback admin user via a second remote /Users call every time a server had no UserId configured. Sources are now fetched in parallel (wall-clock bounded by the slowest source, not their sum), PlaybackInfo responses are cached for 15s to absorb rapid repeat requests, and a fallback-resolved user is remembered for the rest of the server session instead of re-queried on every play. No config or data migration; existing servers, mappings, and watch progress are untouched.
